trends: Today's tech landscape is dominated by the practical application and deep understanding of AI, with a strong emphasis on autonomous agents, local-first processing, and enhanced security. There's a clear move towards empowering AI to directly interact with user interfaces and systems (like iPhone control), but also a critical realization that effective agent implementation requires deterministic, script-like control rather than loose natural language prompting. Data privacy and security, especially concerning third-party AI integrations, are major concerns. Concurrently, there's interest in foundational ML implementations, specialized feature engineering, and making powerful AI tools more accessible through open-source or local alternatives.

ideas.title: AI Agent Workflow Scripting and Orchestration Engine
ideas.description: Inspired by the 'poki' project demonstrating AI agents operating real devices and the Dev.to articles highlighting agent inefficiencies ('talked more than they worked', 'write scripts, not markdown'), this project is a framework for defining and orchestrating deterministic AI agent workflows. Instead of relying on ambiguous natural language prompts for complex tasks, developers can define a sequence of precise, scripted actions (e.g., 'navigate to URL', 'click element X', 'extract text Y', 'process with LLM', 'input Z'). The engine would use a local or API-based LLM for decision-making within pre-defined parameters, executing actions via headless browsers (Playwright/Selenium) or application-specific APIs. This shifts from 'telling' AI to 'programming' AI, improving reliability and auditability of agent tasks.
tech_stack: Local LLM (e.g., Ollama or llama.cpp for privacy/control)
ideas.source_inspiration: poki (GitHub), Don't Write Markdown Files for Your Coding Agent. Write Scripts. (Dev.to), I Gave My Startup 6 AI Employees. They Talked More Than They Worked. (Dev.to)
steps: Task 1: Design a YAML-based DSL for defining agent steps (e.g., `action: navigate`, `target: url`, `extract: selector`).
Task 2: Implement a Python parser for the DSL to interpret workflow definitions.
Task 3: Integrate with a browser automation library (Playwright) to execute defined UI actions.
Task 4: Develop a 'cognitive layer' that interfaces with an LLM for decision points within the workflow (e.g., 'which button to click based on extracted text').
Task 5: Build a simple web UI (Streamlit/Gradio) to upload workflow scripts and monitor agent execution.
Task 6: Create example scripts for common tasks (e.g., web scraping, form filling, data extraction).

ideas.title: Privacy-First Local AI Data Insights Generator
ideas.description: Addressing the 'Fireworks AI security breach' and the general demand for powerful AI tools (like 'Free-ClaudeOpus-5.5') while prioritizing data privacy, this project provides a desktop application for local AI-powered data analysis. Users can upload sensitive documents (PDFs, text files, CSVs) directly to their machine, and a locally-run or self-hosted LLM (e.g., via Ollama/llama.cpp) will process them to generate summaries, extract key entities, answer questions, or identify trends. The key value proposition is that no user data ever leaves the local machine, mitigating risks associated with third-party AI vendors. It acts as a secure, personal AI assistant for sensitive information.
ideas.source_inspiration: Fireworks AI security breach impacts Notion and their customers (Hacker News), secure-pdf-document-processor (GitHub), Free-ClaudeOpus-5.5 (GitHub)
steps: Task 1: Set up a local LLM inference server using Ollama or integrate llama.cpp bindings.
Task 2: Develop a simple web UI (Streamlit or Gradio) for document upload and prompt input.
Task 3: Implement document parsing logic for common formats (PDF, TXT, CSV), converting them into text suitable for LLM input.
Task 4: Create functions to send processed text to the local LLM and display the AI-generated insights/responses.
Task 5: Add features for basic query types (summarization, Q&A, entity extraction).
Task 6: Package the application for easy local deployment (e.g., via PyInstaller or as a Docker container).

ideas.title: Minimalist ML Feature Engineering Toolkit for Time-Series Data
ideas.description: Inspired by 'microgpt's' focus on from-scratch, dependency-free implementations and specialized ML techniques like 'node2vec' and 'imbalanced-dataset-sampler', this project is a lightweight Python library providing highly transparent and efficient feature engineering methods specifically for time-series data. Instead of relying on heavy frameworks, it offers clear, modular functions for generating common time-series features (e.g., rolling averages, lagged values, Fourier transforms, statistical moments) and potentially includes a focused implementation of a sampling technique for imbalanced time-series classification tasks. The emphasis is on readability, control, and a deep understanding of each feature's derivation, making it ideal for developers who want to 'see' how their features are built.
steps: Task 1: Design a core module for basic time-series feature generation (e.g., `calculate_lagged_features`, `compute_rolling_statistics`).
Task 2: Implement more advanced feature transformations (e.g., `fourier_transform_features`, `exponential_smoothing_features`).
Task 3: Develop a specialized data sampler for time-series classification with imbalanced classes (e.g., oversampling minority events while maintaining temporal order).
Task 4: Create clear documentation and examples demonstrating how to use each feature generator with synthetic time-series data.
Task 5: Benchmark the performance and efficiency of the custom implementations against existing libraries where applicable.
Task 6: Structure the library for easy installation and modularity (e.g., using `setuptools`).

quick_actions: Action 1: Experiment with a local LLM setup (e.g., Ollama or llama.cpp) to understand its capabilities and limitations for privacy-sensitive tasks.
Action 2: Spend 1-2 hours scripting a simple UI automation task (e.g., filling a form, scraping specific data) using Playwright or Selenium to grasp deterministic agent control.
Action 3: Reflect on a recent interaction with an AI agent. Identify where a 'scripted' or structured approach could have yielded better, more reliable results than free-form prompting.

Action 4: Before integrating any new third-party AI service or API into a project, make it a habit to skim their data privacy and security policy for 5 minutes, paying attention to data handling and retention.
